title: Task Brief authoring convention and Task Explorer
summary: 106 task entries organize 160 authored variants and 284 imported source records. Every variant has an Overview visual: six source-derived examples and 154 explicitly labeled conceptual drawings. Dataset/target selectors preserve exact contracts, assistance and sources.

decision_provenance: 2026-09-21 user answers: samples now and all tasks eventually; technically literate audience without specialist medical knowledge; existing and proposed tasks with clear draft marking. Other architecture and visual recommendations are by the assistant and await decisions. Later user response “all your rec” accepted shared definition briefs with case indexes, input-first reference reveals, reusable skill plus repository rulebook/template, and separately authoritative executable contracts. User subsequently requested searching and downloading necessary samples. This authorized bounded public data acquisition, not model trials. The user later requested complete brief coverage, then flagged repetitive badges, shared previews and metadata. The assistant refactored presentation to shared task rows with concise case differences and expandable provenance. The user then requested grouping repeated HealthAgentBench tasks and an equivalent AutoMedBench audit. The assistant consolidated dataset/target variants into shared navigation families while retaining individual contracts and source identities. The user explicitly requested further illustrations and authorized original SVG drawings where real examples cannot be downloaded. The assistant added labeled conceptual input/output pictures without treating them as native evidence. The user requested a final independent review and commit. Two read-only reviewers checked navigation and illustration semantics; the assistant fixed their findings, retained image selection captions and separated drawing code from navigation.
reopen_when: When a source revision or task condition changes, a missing case inventory becomes available, or reader feedback demonstrates a needed format change.
